title: Show trunk test scope timing history

intentCoverage.report:
**Caught.** The maintained proof exercises and rejects a timestamp-only change to Project Intent’s observed trunk endpoint. This finding covers that transition; the faulted run stopped before the later stale-reply transition.

Story: `SEED-310#show-trunk-test-scope-timing-history`, from `.planning/seeds/SEED-310-trunk-test-scope-timing-history.md#show-trunk-test-scope-timing-history` and plan `.planning/slice-plans/581-show-trunk-test-scope-timing-history/PLAN.md`, at completed implementation revision `e37801b5c98285c8558deace0ca5be5d9ad5024e`. The selected promise is stable endpoint observation freshness for an unchanged configured source/revision: a newer snapshot retrieval time alone must neither change the endpoint date nor read history again.

One fault was introduced in the isolated detached checkout `/private/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-SEED-310-live.O2VzuF/checkout`: `dashboard/src/IntentCiEvidence.tsx:65`, in `useObservedTrunkEndpoint`, changed `return observed.endpoint;` to `return endpoint;`. This plausibly substitutes snapshot retrieval time for the remembered observation time. Maintained fixtures and assertions were unchanged.

All three runs used `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH caffeinate -s -i npm run test:dashboard -- dashboard/frontend-tests/intent-project-scope-history-key-isolation.spec.ts --workers=1`. The maintained case at line 20 mounts the real evidence provider using `comparisonMountPage.ts`, `summaryScopeFacts()` and MakeMe published-work arrangements, then changes only `work.retrievedAt` from `2026-11-11T07:00:00Z` to `2026-11-11T07:02:00Z` while revision remains forty `a` characters.

- Baseline: exit 0; proof record completed, one executed test passed, strict status passed.
- Fault: exit 1; proof record completed, one executed test failed, strict status failed. The catching assertion is `history.locator("time").first()).toHaveAttribute("datetime", "2026-11-11T07:00:00.000Z")` at `dashboard/frontend-tests/intent-project-scope-history-key-isolation.spec.ts:80`. It received `2026-11-11T07:02:00.000Z`. The following request-count assertion was not reached.
- Independent wrong-behavior observation: parsing the retained browser trace’s frame snapshots, separately from its assertion verdict, found actual TIME elements first at `07:00:00.000Z`, then at `07:02:00.000Z`. Its network snapshots contain two scope-history requests with the identical revision and scope `dashboard/tests`, but `through=2026-11-11T07:00:00.000Z` and then `through=2026-11-11T07:02:00.000Z`. This establishes both the manufactured observation date and the unwanted same-head history read on the maintained path.
- Restoration: an EXIT/INT/TERM restoration arrangement protected the edit. Byte comparison matched the original source, Git status matched the initially clean scratch state, and the same command then passed: exit 0, completed proof record, one executed test passed, strict status passed. Final Git status was clean. The live execution checkout was not edited; nothing was committed or pushed.

Evidence remains under `/private/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-SEED-310-live.O2VzuF`: `baseline-proof.json`, `fault-proof.json`, `restored-proof.json`, corresponding logs and wall measurements, and `independent-trace-observation.json`. The trace is under `checkout/dashboard/test-results/2026-11-11T10-09-39.049Z-87687/frontend-tests-intent-proj-afc08--cannot-replace-the-new-one-chromium/trace.zip`.

**Next proof action:** retain the existing datetime assertion and request-count proof for this promise. This check supports no new test repair. It matches the plan’s existing same-head timestamp/no time-only-read protection; recognition of that protection is separate from the caller’s disposition and closure.

Execution followed the project’s [failing and flaky test policy](/Users/terryyin/git/open-dough/.worktrees/show-trunk-test-scope-timing-history/AGENTS.md#failing-and-flaky-tests). Native isolated npm/browser setup and prerequisite validation passed with Node 24.21.0 and Chromium 153.0.8010.12. Immediately before proof the host reported AC power, 100% charge, load averages 3.88/5.89/9.02 and 46% free memory; proof used one worker and the maintained `caffeinate -s -i` guard. No sleeps, timeout changes, broad suite, repeated probe, or guidance changes were used.

- **Test runtime.** Measured runner durations from proof-record `terminal.durationMs`: baseline 4,547.288 ms; fault 6,663.538 ms; restored 1,527.100 ms; total 12,737.926 ms. Recorded test-attempt durations were respectively 290 ms, 5,257 ms and 255 ms, total 5,802 ms. Measured command wall intervals totalled 14,176 ms; these are distinct from runner and test execution time.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: no separate human-work measurement was supplied or observed; elapsed time is not a human-effort measure.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable: no independently measured host agent usage or active-effort figure is available to this worker; elapsed time and test runtime are not substitutes.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 137206 ms (measured), from 1794391689341 to 1794391826547 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision: `e37801b5c98285c8558deace0ca5be5d9ad5024e`.

Accepted the worker's terminal report for the unchanged-head timestamp transition. Its baseline and restored maintained check passed, the faulted assertion caught the wrong datetime, and separate trace snapshots established both the changed observation date and the unwanted same-head read. The faulted run did not reach the later stale-reply transition; this one probe makes no whole-story protection claim.

Decision: retain the existing datetime assertion and request-count proof. No test repair or new correction is supported by this result; a deliberate scratch fault is not a delivered defect. No retrospective follow-up exists and no new follow-up is queued. Canonical follow-up links: none.

Subsequent closure edits concern documentation and records, preserving the checked promise and proof. The worker joined via its native completion notification while independent wrap-up ran; no duplicate worker, restart, status polling or overdue recovery was needed. Original local evidence paths remain in the verbatim report; maintained source/tests/policy are recoverable at the checked revision.
